newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 92 +2 on last week
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 136 n/c on last week
AMLC COMMENTARY: The major market development during the week was good rains over much of Australia.
A wide belt stretching from the Western Australia coast through South Australia to central New South Wales and Queensland saw 10-25mm of rains.
In Queensland, some of the rain fell as hail, damaging crop. However in Southern and central parts of the state, the rain represented much-needed good news for cattle producers.

Cow prices were weaker. Korean steer and Japan bullock prices were weaker in Victoria, while in other states no clear trend was evident. Mixed results in cattle markets contrasted with generally better prices in export markets. In the U.S., after falling from 200 c/kg in mid-August to 186c/kg in mid-September, export prices for 90CL grinding beef have recovered much of the lost ground to finish this week at 195c/kg.

Beef prices in Japan also continue to rise. For a number of chilled cuts, wholesale beef prices in Japan are at record highs for this year. Chilled grassfed fullsets sold this week for 580 Yen/kg, up 25 yen/kg from last week.

The U.S. manufacturing beef market moved higher this week for both domestic and imported product. The driving factor as a big drop-off in the fed cattle slaughter rate. The week ended September 28 saw U.S. beef production down over 15 percent from year-earlier levels.
